newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Liechtenstein LGT shuffles top management.
newsitem.headline: Liechtenstein LGT shuffles top management.

text.p: Private bank and fund manager Liechtenstein Global Trust AG (LGT) said it had reorganised top management following the acquisition of New York-based Chancellor Capital Management Inc.

LGT said the board of directors had been cut down from 14 to five members, including chairman and chief executive Prince Philipp von und zu Liechtenstein, in order to maintain felxibility and marekt orientation.

It said an advisory board had also been formed including senior members of Chancellor Capital Management, which LGT acquired last month, increasing its assets under management to more than $80 billion.
The advisory board is also chaired by Prince Philipp and has 17 other members, including Warren Shaw, who was Chancellor's president and chief executive before the sale.
Shaw had headed a management group that owned 51 percent of Chancellor before the LGT deal.
LGT said the combination of a small, focused board of directors and a broad-based advisory board seemed to be the right way to meet the challenges of global asset management and private banking.
